chunks: "I've used [tool(s)] on [N] boards. The one I'm proudest of is [project: e. g. a four-layer motor controller with an STM32, a gate driver and USB] .
I did it end to end: I created the symbols and footprints from the datasheets, drew a hierarchical schematic, ran ERC, then did the layout. A few decisions I can walk through.
I used a four-layer stackup with a ground plane directly under the top layer so the return paths were short. I set net classes: signals at 0.
15 mm, power traces sized from the current, and I used the IPC-2221 charts to size the 2 amps motor supply trace to about 0. 8 mm on an outer layer for a 10 degree rise.
I routed USB as a 90 ohm differential pair against the plane, matched the lengths, and kept it away from the switching node.
I put decoupling capacitors on the same side as the pins, with vias right at the capacitor pads.
For checking, I ran DRC with the fab's minimum rules, reviewed the Gerbers in a separate viewer, and had a classmate review the schematic against the datasheets.
At bring-up I found [an error, e. g. a mirrored footprint] , which I fixed with a bodge wire and corrected in the library. My weaker areas are [e. g.
DDR, RF, and scripting] , which I'd like to learn."
